scenario: [LTIM.10.7] with [LTIM.10.9]'s overlap: the facts of one zone may overlap, and the one with the greatest `valid_from` not after the instant decides, whatever order they arrived in. Two `Europe/Paris` rows, the later one asserted first: B, +7200, from 2024-03-01T00:00Z until 2024-06-01T00:00Z; then A, +3600, from 2024-01-01T00:00Z until 2025-01-01T00:00Z. Event 1 at 2024-04-01T09:00Z falls in both: B has the greater `valid_from`, so Paris reads 11:00 and `b_wins` fires while `a_wins` (10:00) does not. Event 2 at 2024-07-01T09:00Z is still covered by A, but B has the greatest `valid_from` not after it and B's `valid_until` has passed, so the zone has no answer there ([LTIM.10.7]: "Otherwise ... `Z` has no answer at `t`"). The read faults DOMAIN and `covered` does not fire. Exactly ['b']. PATH PINNED: the per-zone index's predecessor lookup, libds's `ds_rete_tz_resolve` and Mercury's `ds.wm` index read by `ds.eval`.
rules_ds:
schema Event scope logical:
    id: Int key
    seen: Time mutable

rule b_wins:
    Event e where e.id == 1 and e.seen.local("Europe/Paris").hour == 11
->
    log critical "b"

rule a_wins:
    Event e where e.id == 1 and e.seen.local("Europe/Paris").hour == 10
->
    log critical "a"

rule covered:
    Event e where e.id == 2 and e.seen.local("Europe/Paris").hour >= 0
->
    log critical "covered"
